subject: Calisto7b elevated 503/timeouts — BrightLeaf SRE escalation & next steps
messages:
From: Clara Zhou <clara@brightleaf.ai>

Cc: BrightLeaf SRE <sre@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: urgent: spikes of 503s from calisto7b since 08:45 PST

Hi Kimberly —

We started seeing elevated 503 / timeout responses from model calisto7b hitting our inference endpoints starting ~08:45 PST. Error rate is roughly 18% on traffic routed to calisto7b (request IDs attached). Example request IDs: r-8f3a2, r-8f3a9, r-8f3d0. Attached is a trimmed server log and a short snippet from our side showing the failing requests (calisto7b-error-sample-logs.txt).

Can you confirm whether this is something on Redwood's side? We're in the middle of a large batch and this is causing downstream retries on our end. If there's a recommended fallback or short-term mitigation, please advise — we can try routing to a different model if necessary.

Thanks — this is blocking a scheduled batch run.

— Clara

From: markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.com>, BrightLeaf SRE <sre@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Nov 2028 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: urgent: spikes of 503s from calisto7b since 08:45 PST

We triaged: preliminary findings below. (INF-4721 created)

Summary:
- Symptoms: elevated 503s and hard timeouts from calisto7b serving pool on two availability zones (az-us-west-2a, az-us-west-2b). Error surface matches OOM/retry behavior in the runtime (KV cache eviction thrashing + occasional segfaults in a kernel path).
- Trigger conditions: traffic containing long multi-turn histories with repeated large embeddings (seen in BrightLeaf sample) spikes memory usage in the calisto7b K/V cache path after a recent runtime optimization that changed chunking for attention keys.

Immediate actions (already executed):
- Rolled a targeted restart of the affected calisto7b worker group (completed 09:25 PST).
- Applied temporary throttling on sequence length for calisto7b for accounts routing through the affected shards (this reduces throughput but prevents crashes).
- Opened INF-4721 and attached a heaptrace + screenshot (INF-4721-screenshot.png).

Short-term mitigation for BrightLeaf: we recommend routing your traffic to calisto7b-quant (lower mem footprint) while we validate the patch. If you want us to flip the routing for your account, we can do it now.

Next steps / timeline:
- Build & validation of runtime patch to guard the KV cache allocation path (ETA 48–72 hours).
- Canary rollout of the patch across calisto7b shards (24 hours after validation).
- Postmortem + remediation doc (link to draft once available).

Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Software Engineer, Model Runtime
markus@redwood.com

From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Clara Zhou <clara@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Nov 2028 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Calisto7b incident — preliminary postmortem and next steps

Hi Clara —

Thanks again for the quick routing change; glad the quant fallback reduced your error surface. This is a brief preliminary postmortem and plan while the engineering team completes validation. Full postmortem PDF is attached (postmortem-calisto7b-draft.pdf) and the Jira for tracking is INF-4721.

What happened (tl;dr):
- Between 08:45–09:20 PST on 2028-11-02 we observed elevated 503s from calisto7b caused by an edge-case allocation path in the runtime KV cache after a recent optimization. Under long sequence workloads with repeated embeddings the allocation path triggered excessive eviction/resizing which led to instability and occasional process failures.

Impact for BrightLeaf:
- Peak error rate: ~18% for traffic hitting the affected shards.
- You observed issues from ~08:45–09:25 PST; your routing change to calisto7b-quant brought errors down to acceptable levels.

Immediate remediation we executed:
- Targeted restart of affected workers (09:25 PST).
- Temporary throttling on sequence length for affected shards.
- Provided account-level routing change to calisto7b-quant for BrightLeaf.

Permanent fix and timeline:
- Patch: add guard checks and a preallocation cap in the KV cache allocation path to avoid eviction thrashing (development complete).
- Validation: unit + load tests (in progress) and canary validation in two AZs (scheduled; ETA 36–48 hours).
- Rollout: staged rollout across calisto7b cluster after successful canary (expected 72 hours to full roll).

Compensation & follow-up:
- We'll issue a one-time credit for the impacted window once the incident is closed. Ben (cc) will coordinate billing adjustments.
- We'll schedule the 30-minute review with your SRE team after the draft is finalized — does Tue, Nov 7 at 10:00 PST work?

Links & tickets:
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4721
- Draft postmortem (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/fakepostmortem

Attachments included:
- postmortem-calisto7b-draft.pdf
- INF-4721-screenshot.png (heaptrace snippet)
- calisto7b-error-sample-logs.txt (customer-submitted)

If you'd prefer a direct routing change back to calisto7b once we finish canarying, we can coordinate a narrow window with you.

Apologies again for the interruption — we take these regressions seriously and will share the final postmortem and validation results as soon as available.

— Kimberly
